coverage.note: Every CT post in the WFP post sitemap for 2022-2026 was listed; slate, primary, governor and results posts were opened. Municipal, statewide-office and policy posts were screened by title. The 2026 candidate list (76 CT rows including Lamont) was read from the saved national file. CT WFP cross-endorses by nominating, so each name on a slate counts as a WFP ballot-line endorsement. No endorsement for a special election found. Town-committee pages were not checked.

The national site's CT category holds one post (Angie Parkinson, 2026). No 2022 or 2024 CT endorsement found there. Local Our Revolution chapters in Connecticut were not enumerated, so the status is blocked.

The saved national DSA tables hold one CT row (Justin Farmer SD17, 2020), out of scope. The chapter site shows no 2022-2026 state endorsements in the pages read. Chapter social feeds, branch pages and the 2026 gubernatorial analysis post were not checked for endorsements.

Read from the saved directory cards (research_notes/State endorsement gap review/rfs_pccc_directory_cards.tsv) and each card's profile page. Entries: 2022 5, 2024 5, 2026 3. 2020 cards are out of scope. Stage for 2026 uses the dated RFS press releases in the saved release table.
Only champions lists were reachable; they are not endorsements and name no CT state legislator. 2024 and 2026 state pages were not found on the issuer site.

Sunrise Movement Connecticut posted 2024 endorsements as images (3 legislative). No 2022 or 2026 list found. Other hubs were inaccessible or had no endorsement page in the saved review, so the status is blocked.

gaps: 2026 general (2026-11-03) results are not in the official database. electionhistory.ct.gov lists contests through the 2026-09-01 primary only, and the Secretary of the State's election-night site (https://ctemspublic.pcctg.net/) renders with JavaScript and gives no citable text. Every 2026 endorsee is therefore 'pending' (primary results are in notes). CT WFP's own post of 2026-11-04 (https://workingfamilies.org/2026/11/connecticut-working-families-party-flips-and-defends-seats-across-the-state-builds-toward-working-families-governing-majority-at-the-capitol/) names claimed winners (Fernandez HD-48, Kiner SD-7, Wisialowski HD-23, Cardillo HD-83, Carelus HD-31, Marx SD-20, Menapace HD-37, Gauthier HD-38, Shannon HD-117, Shake HD-120, Martinez HD-22) but it is the issuer's claim, not a results source, so it was not used. Re-run after certification to set outcome, result_source and current (term 2027-01-06 per Conn. Const. art. III sec. 10 and art. IV sec. 2).

Possible term-length change for 2026 winners: a web search surfaced 2025 Senate Joint Resolution 14, which would lengthen legislative terms and was said to go to voters on 2026-11-03. I did not confirm that it is on the ballot or passed. If it passed, term_end for 2026 winners (and possibly sitting members) needs re-checking against the constitution.

Official result excerpts are taken from the JSON embedded in each electionhistory.ct.gov contest page (the visible page text renders client-side, so the vote table is not in the page text). The excerpt shows the endorsee's own vote count; the winner and other counts are in notes and in the same embedded data (isWinner). Pages could not be cross-checked against the SOTS statement of vote PDFs.

WFP 2024 slate (https://workingfamilies.org/2024/09/connecticut-working-families-party-endorses-85-candidates-ahead-of-the-november-election/): title says 84 candidates, URL says 85, and the page lists 3 federal candidates plus 62 House and 18 Senate rows (80 state rows). The June 2024 announcement (7 candidates) adds Tyler Mack SD22, Brandon Chafee HD33 and Abdul Osmanu HD94, who are not in the September list. Total state entries for 2024: 84. The headline count was not reconciled.
Charneil Bush (SD15, WFP 2022) is outcome 'unknown': he is not on the 2022 general ballot and no 2022 primary contest for the seat lists him, so the reason he did not appear is not sourced.

WFP stage: the 76 rows of the 2026 national list are undated. Six were announced 2026-06-16 (primary); the other 70 default to stage 'general'. Some were probably announced before the 2026-08-11 primary.

CT WFP page 'Joe de la Cruz: Fighting for Working Families in Connecticut' (2026-09-01) is paid for by 'Working Families for Education Excellence', an independent-expenditure group, not the party. It opposes Heather Somers for State Senate. Treated as not an endorsement by WFP; no entry.
